opener: Father, I need to say the honest thing out loud instead of just thinking it: I'm tired of asking You the same question every morning — how much longer? Little by little feels impossibly slow when I need this fixed today.
paragraphs: I keep measuring my progress against everybody else's finish line, and it makes the ground I've actually gained feel like nothing at all. The bill still unpaid, the apology that still hasn't come, the body still healing, the dream still just a draft on a page — none of it looks like deliverance yet, and some days the gap between where I am and where I thought I'd be by now presses harder on my chest than the actual problem does. I don't need another lecture on patience. I need to know You haven't forgotten the promise.

So today I am trading my timeline for Yours, because Your record has never once needed to rush to be faithful. You moved a whole nation out of bondage one step, one fight, one little victory at a time, and You called every single step deliverance — never delay. I believe You are doing that exact same work in me right now, clearing out what has to go before I can carry what I'm asking for. Teach me to stop confusing Your pace with Your absence. I may not see the whole promise yet, but I can see today's inch of ground, and today I choose to thank You for it instead of resenting it for not being a mile. In Jesus' name, amen.
bold: stop confusing Your pace with Your absence
footerNote: Save this for the next time "little by little" feels like "not at all"
